```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Fits and compares CART, Bagging, Random Forest and XGBoost to classify students as Dropout / Enrolled / Graduate (thesis Chapter 7).
Requires `data/prepared_data.rds`, created by `01_data_preparation.Rmd`.

Load the required libraries.

```{r}
library(caTools)
library(dplyr)
library(corrplot)
library(nnet)
library(pheatmap)
library(xgboost)
library(gbm)
library(caret)
library(cvms)
library(randomForest)
library(tree)
```

Load the prepared data (full dataset and train / validation / test sets).

```{r}
prepared <- readRDS("data/prepared_data.rds")
data_new   <- prepared$data_new
train      <- prepared$train
validation <- prepared$validation
test       <- prepared$test
```

# CART (baseline)

Fit a classification tree (Gini criterion).

```{r}
tree <- tree(train$Target ~. ,data= train ,method = 'gini')
summary(tree)
```

Plot the full tree.

```{r}
plot(tree,col='darkgray',lwd=2)
text(tree,pretty=0,col='blue',cex=0.6)
```

## Tree pruning

Cross-validation (misclassification error) to choose the tree size.

```{r}
tree

cv.diabetes <- cv.tree(tree, FUN=prune.misclass)

names(cv.diabetes)
cv.diabetes
```

Prune the tree to the best size found (7 terminal nodes).

```{r}
prune.diabetes <- prune.tree(tree,best=7, method = "misclass")
prune.diabetes
```

Predict on the test set and compute the confusion matrix.

```{r}
tree_pred = predict(prune.diabetes, test, type = "class")
confusion_matrix_tree= confusionMatrix(data=tree_pred,test$Target)
print(confusion_matrix_tree)
```

Plot the normalized confusion matrix (percentages by actual class).

```{r}
confusion_tree_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(confusion_matrix_tree))
colnames(confusion_tree_df) <- c("Predicted", "Reference", "Count")

# Sum for the actual labels
sums <- tapply(confusion_tree_df$Count, confusion_tree_df$Reference, sum)

# Percentages
confusion_tree_df$Percentage <- confusion_tree_df$Count / sums[confusion_tree_df$Reference] * 100

ggplot(confusion_tree_df, aes(x = Reference, y = Predicted, fill = Percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "purple") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Actual", y = "Predicted", title = "Normalized Confusion Matrix")

```

# Bagging

Bagging = random forest with `mtry` equal to the number of predictors (27).

```{r}
set.seed(1234)
bag = randomForest(Target ~ ., data = train, mtry = 27, importance = TRUE,
                            ntree = 1000, type="classification")
bag
```

## Bagging predictions

```{r}
predictions_bag = predict(bag, newdata = test)
confusion_matrix_bag= confusionMatrix(data=predictions_bag, test$Target)
print(confusion_matrix_bag)
```

## Bagging variable importance

Top 15 variables by Mean Decrease in Gini.

```{r}

  bag,
  main = "Top 15 Variable Importance (Bagging)",
  n.var = 15,  # Display top 10 variables
  pch= 16,
  type = 2,  # Use Mean Decrease in Gini
  col = "purple"  # Customize bar color to purple
)

```

Print the top 3 variables.

```{r}
importance_values <- importance(bag)

# Sort by Mean Decrease in Gini
importance_gini <- importance_values[ , "MeanDecreaseGini"]
importance_sorted <- sort(importance_gini, decreasing = TRUE)

# Display the top 3 variables
top_3_gini <- head(importance_sorted, 3)
print(top_3_gini)

# Optional: View the top 3 in a more readable format
cat("Top 3 Variables by Mean Decrease in Gini:\n")
for (var in names(top_3_gini)) {
  cat(sprintf("%s: %.3f\n", var, top_3_gini[var]))
}
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Ensure the target variable is a factor
train$Target <- as.factor(train$Target)

# Train the Gradient Boosting model
gbm_model <- gbm(
  formula = Target ~ ., 
  data = train, 
  distribution = "multinomial", 
  n.trees = 1000, 
  interaction.depth = 4, 
  shrinkage = 0.01, 
  cv.folds = 5
)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(caret)

# Create the confusion matrix
```

# XGBoost

## Data for XGBoost

Re-split the data into train (80%) and test (20%).
The test set is the same as above (same seed); `train` here is the 80% that remains after removing the test set, so it also contains the validation rows.

```{r}
data_new$Target = as.factor(data_new$Target)

n = nrow(data_new)

set.seed(1234)

# Test set (20% of the data)
select_test = sample(1:n, n * 0.2)
test = as.data.frame(data_new[select_test, ])

# Training set (remaining 80%)
train = as.data.frame(data_new[-select_test, ])

cat("Training set dimensions: ", dim(train), "\n")
cat("Test set dimensions: ", dim(test), "\n")
```

Check the class distribution, then build the numeric design matrices (dummy variables for the categorical predictors, target excluded) and the numeric labels (0, 1, 2) required by XGBoost.

```{r}
# Example: Split data into training and validation sets and test

table(train$Target)
table(test$Target)

X_train <- model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = train[, -ncol(train)])  # Exclude the target column
X_test <- model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = test[, - ncol(test)])    # Exclude the target column
X_validation <- model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = validation[, - ncol(validation)])    # Exclude the target column
# Step 2: Convert the target variable to numeric format
y_train <- as.numeric(as.factor(train$Target)) - 1
y_test <- as.numeric(as.factor(test$Target)) - 1
y_validation <-  as.numeric(as.factor(validation$Target)) - 1
```

Class weights for the imbalanced classes: inverse of each class frequency in the training set.

```{r}
# Set scale_pos_weight based on the inverse frequency of each class
dropout_weight <- nrow(train) / sum(train$Target == "Dropout")
enrolled_weight <- nrow(train) / sum(train$Target == "Enrolled")
graduate_weight <- nrow(train) / sum(train$Target == "Graduate")

# Define a named vector for the scale_pos_weight to assign to each class
scale_pos_weights <- c("Dropout" = dropout_weight, 
                       "Enrolled" = enrolled_weight, 
                       "Graduate" = graduate_weight)
```

Convert the matrices to XGBoost's `DMatrix` format.

```{r}
xgb_train <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
xgb_test <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test, label = y_test)
xgb_validation <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_validation, label = y_validation)
```

## Hyperparameter tuning (stepwise strategy)

Parameters are tuned one step at a time (one or two parameters per step) with 5-fold cross-validation on the training set, minimizing the multiclass log-loss. The best value found at each step is kept fixed in the following ones (approach of Islam et al., 2021; thesis Chapter 7.6.2).

Starting point: the default XGBoost parameters.

```{r}
fixed_params <- list(
  booster = "gbtree",             # Type of booster (gbtree or dart)
  eta = 0.3,                      # Learning rate, default
  max_depth = 6,                  # default
  min_child_weight = 1,           # Minimum sum of weights in child nodes, default
  gamma = 0,                      # Minimum loss reduction to split, default
  max_delta_step = 0,             # DEFAULT
  subsample = 1,                  # Subsample ratio of training examples, default
  colsample_bytree = 1,           # Subsample ratio of columns, default
  lambda = 1,                     # default
  scale_pos_weight = c(dropout_weight, enrolled_weight, graduate_weight),                            
  alpha = 0,                      # default
  objective = "multi:softprob",   # Objective function for multi-class classification
  eval_metric = "mlogloss",       # Evaluation metric
  num_class = length(unique(y_train)) # Number of classes
)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
help("xgboost")
```

### Step 1: number of boosting rounds (`nrounds`)

```{r}
# Step 1: Tune `nrounds` (equivalent to `n_estimators`)
set.seed(1234)
param_grid_step1 <- expand.grid(nrounds = seq(1000, 20000, 3000))

result_step1 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 20) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_nrounds <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(nrounds = integer(), logloss = numeric())  # Initialize the results data frame

  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing nrounds = %d\n", i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$nrounds[i]))
    current_nrounds <- param_grid$nrounds[i]
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = fixed_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = current_nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )

    # Extract the minimum logloss from the evaluation log
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean, na.rm = TRUE)  # Added `na.rm = TRUE` for safety
    
    # Append the results to logloss_results
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, data.frame(nrounds = current_nrounds, logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    # Update the best parameters if a lower logloss is found
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_nrounds <- current_nrounds
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (nrounds = %d)\n", best_logloss, best_nrounds))
    }
  }

  # Return all results, including the logloss_results
  list(best_nrounds = best_nrounds, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}


# Run the optimization for `nrounds`
result_step1 <- result_step1(param_grid_step1, fixed_params, xgb_train)

# Update the number of rounds in the fixed parameters
cat(sprintf("\nBest number of rounds: %d, Logloss: %.4f\n", result_step1$best_nrounds, result_step1$best_logloss))
nrounds <- result_step1$best_nrounds  # Needed in the following steps

# Extract results for plotting
logloss_results <- result_step1$logloss_results
best_nrounds <- result_step1$best_nrounds
best_logloss <- result_step1$best_logloss

# Plot 
ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = nrounds, y = logloss)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_nrounds, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-Validation Logloss vs. nrounds",
    x = "nrounds",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  annotate("text", x = best_nrounds, y = min(logloss_results$logloss), 
           label = paste("Best nrounds =", best_nrounds), 
           vjust = -1, hjust = -0.1, color = "red", size = 3.5)
logloss_results
```

### Step 2: tree complexity (`max_depth`, `min_child_weight`)

```{r}
# Step 2: Tune `max_depth` and `min_child_weight`
set.seed(1234)
param_grid_step2 <- expand.grid(max_depth = c(1, 4 , 8), min_child_weight = c(1, 3, 6))

result_step2 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(max_depth = integer(), 
                                 min_child_weight = integer(), 
                                 logloss = numeric())

  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing max_depth = %d, min_child_weight = %d\n", 
                i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$max_depth[i], param_grid$min_child_weight[i]))
    
    current_params <- list(
      max_depth = param_grid$max_depth[i],
      min_child_weight = param_grid$min_child_weight[i]
    )
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search params
    params <- c(fixed_params, current_params)
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, 
                             data.frame(max_depth = current_params$max_depth, 
                                        min_child_weight = current_params$min_child_weight, 
                                        logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- current_params
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (max_depth = %d, min_child_weight = %d)\n", 
                  best_logloss, best_params$max_depth, best_params$min_child_weight))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}

# Run the optimization for `max_depth` and `min_child_weight`
result_step2 <- result_step2(param_grid_step2, fixed_params, xgb_train, nrounds = nrounds)

# Extract results for plotting
logloss_results <- result_step2$logloss_results
best_params <- result_step2$best_params
best_logloss <- result_step2$best_logloss

# Update the parameters with the best found values
cat(sprintf("\nBest parameters: max_depth = %d, min_child_weight = %d, Logloss: %.4f\n", 
            best_params$max_depth, 
            best_params$min_child_weight, 
            best_logloss))

fixed_params$max_depth <- best_params$max_depth
fixed_params$min_child_weight <- best_params$min_child_weight
```

Plot log-loss for each (`max_depth`, `min_child_weight`) combination.

```{r}
logloss_results$param_combination <- paste0(logloss_results$max_depth, ".", logloss_results$min_child_weight)

best_index <- which.min(logloss_results$logloss)
best_combination <- logloss_results$param_combination[best_index]
best_logloss <- logloss_results$logloss[best_index]

ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = param_combination, y = logloss, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  # Line plot for log-loss
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Add points to the line
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(factor(best_combination, levels = logloss_results$param_combination)), 
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Highlight best combination
  annotate("text", 
           x = as.numeric(factor(best_combination, levels = logloss_results$param_combination)), 
           y = best_logloss, 
           label = paste("Best:", best_combination), 
           vjust = -1, hjust = -0.1, color = "red", size = 4) +  # Label for best combination
  labs(
    title = "Logloss vs. Parameter Combinations",
    x = "Parameter Combinations (max_depth and min_child_weight)",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Same plot, with the dashed line aligned to the best combination.

```{r}
best_index <- which.min(logloss_results$logloss)
best_combination <- logloss_results$param_combination[best_index]
best_logloss <- logloss_results$logloss[best_index]

# Ensure the dashed line aligns with the best combination
ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = param_combination, y = logloss, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  # Line plot for log-loss
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Add points to the line
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = as.numeric(factor(logloss_results$param_combination))[best_index], 
    color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1
  ) +  # Correct alignment with best combination
  annotate("text", 
           x = as.numeric(factor(logloss_results$param_combination))[best_index], 
           y = best_logloss, 
           label = paste("Best:", best_combination), 
           vjust = -1, hjust = -0.1, color = "red", size = 4) +  # Correct label for best combination
  labs(
    title = "Logloss vs. Parameter Combinations",
    x = "Parameter Combinations (max_depth ; min_child_weight)",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Step 3: minimum loss reduction to split (`gamma`)

Check the best parameters so far.

```{r}
fixed_params
fixed_params[["eta"]] <- 0.3
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Tune `gamma`
set.seed(1234)
param_grid_step3 <- expand.grid(gamma = c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 
                                        4))

result_step3 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(gamma = numeric(), logloss = numeric())  # Initialize the results data frame

  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing gamma = %.2f\n", i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$gamma[i]))
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search param
    current_params <- list(
      booster = fixed_params$booster,
      eta = fixed_params$eta,
      max_depth = fixed_params$max_depth,
      min_child_weight = fixed_params$min_child_weight,
      subsample = fixed_params$subsample,
      colsample_bytree = fixed_params$colsample_bytree,
      objective = fixed_params$objective,
      eval_metric = fixed_params$eval_metric,
      num_class = fixed_params$num_class,
      gamma = param_grid$gamma[i]  # Dynamically set gamma
    )
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = current_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, data.frame(gamma = param_grid$gamma[i], logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- current_params
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (gamma = %.2f)\n", best_logloss, param_grid$gamma[i]))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}

# Run the optimization for `gamma`
result_step3 <- result_step3(param_grid_step3, fixed_params, xgb_train, nrounds = nrounds)

# Extract results for plotting
logloss_results <- result_step3$logloss_results
best_gamma <- result_step3$best_params$gamma
best_logloss <- result_step3$best_logloss

# Update the parameters with the best found value
cat(sprintf("\nBest parameter: gamma = %.2f, Logloss: %.4f\n", best_gamma, best_logloss))

fixed_params$gamma <- best_gamma

# Plot the results
ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = gamma, y = logloss)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  # Line plot for log-loss
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Points for each gamma value
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_gamma, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Highlight best gamma
  annotate("text", x = best_gamma, y = best_logloss, 
           label = paste("Best: gamma =", best_gamma), 
           vjust = -1, hjust = -0.1, color = "red", size = 4) +  # Label for best gamma
  labs(
    title = "Logloss vs. Gamma",
    x = "Gamma",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Step 4: randomness (`subsample`, `colsample_bytree`)

```{r}
fixed_params
```

```{r}
set.seed(
  1234
)
param_grid_step4 <- expand.grid(subsample = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1), colsample_bytree = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1))
set.seed(1234)
result_step4 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(subsample = numeric(), colsample_bytree = numeric(), logloss = numeric())

  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing subsample = %.1f, colsample_bytree = %.1f\n", 
                i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$subsample[i], param_grid$colsample_bytree[i]))
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search params
    current_params <- list(
      booster = fixed_params$booster,
      eta = fixed_params$eta,
      max_depth = fixed_params$max_depth,
      min_child_weight = fixed_params$min_child_weight,
      gamma = fixed_params$gamma,
      objective = fixed_params$objective,
      eval_metric = fixed_params$eval_metric,
      num_class = fixed_params$num_class,
      subsample = param_grid$subsample[i],                # Dynamically set subsample
      colsample_bytree = param_grid$colsample_bytree[i]   # Dynamically set colsample_bytree
    )
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = current_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, 
                             data.frame(subsample = param_grid$subsample[i], 
                                        colsample_bytree = param_grid$colsample_bytree[i], 
                                        logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- current_params
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (subsample = %.1f, colsample_bytree = %.1f)\n", 
                  best_logloss, param_grid$subsample[i], param_grid$colsample_bytree[i]))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}
set.seed(1234)
# Run the updated optimization for `subsample` and `colsample_bytree`
result_step4 <- result_step4(param_grid_step4, fixed_params, xgb_train, nrounds = nrounds)

# Extract results for plotting
logloss_results <- result_step4$logloss_results
logloss_results$combination <- paste(logloss_results$subsample, logloss_results$colsample_bytree, sep = "-")

best_subsample <- result_step4$best_params$subsample
best_colsample_bytree <- result_step4$best_params$colsample_bytree
best_logloss <- result_step4$best_logloss

# Update the parameters with the best found values
cat(sprintf("\nBest parameters: subsample = %.1f, colsample_bytree = %.1f, Logloss: %.4f\n", 
            best_subsample, best_colsample_bytree, best_logloss))

fixed_params$subsample <- best_subsample
fixed_params$colsample_bytree <- best_colsample_bytree

# Plot the results as a line plot

ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = combination, y = logloss, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  # Line plot for log-loss
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Points for each combination
  geom_vline(xintercept = which.min(logloss_results$logloss), color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Highlight best combination
  annotate("text", x = which.min(logloss_results$logloss), y = best_logloss, 
           label = paste("Best:   ", best_subsample, best_colsample_bytree), 
           vjust = -1, color = "red", size = 4) +  # Label for best combination
  labs(
    title = "Logloss vs. Parameter Combination",
    x = "Combination (subsample ; colsample_bytree)",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Step 5: regularization (`alpha`, `lambda`)

Make the model more conservative with L1 (`alpha`) and L2 (`lambda`) regularization.

```{r}
param_grid_step5 <- expand.grid(alpha = c(0, 0.5, 1), lambda = c(1, 1.5, 2))
set.seed(1234)
result_step5 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- list()
  logloss_results <- data.frame(alpha = numeric(), lambda = numeric(), logloss = numeric())
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing alpha = %.1f, lambda = %.1f\n", 
                i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$alpha[i], param_grid$lambda[i]))
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search params
    current_params <- c(
      fixed_params,
      list(
        alpha = param_grid$alpha[i],   # Dynamically set alpha
        lambda = param_grid$lambda[i] # Dynamically set lambda
      )
    )
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = current_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, 
                             data.frame(alpha = param_grid$alpha[i], 
                                        lambda = param_grid$lambda[i], 
                                        logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    # Ensure the best_logloss and corresponding parameters are stored
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- list(alpha = param_grid$alpha[i], lambda = param_grid$lambda[i])
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (alpha = %.1f, lambda = %.1f)\n", 
                  best_logloss, param_grid$alpha[i], param_grid$lambda[i]))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}

# Run the optimization for `alpha` and `lambda`
result_step5 <- result_step5(param_grid_step5, fixed_params, xgb_train, nrounds = nrounds)

# Extract results for plotting
logloss_results <- result_step5$logloss_results
logloss_results$combination <- paste(logloss_results$alpha, logloss_results$lambda, sep = "-")

best_alpha <- result_step5$best_params$alpha
best_lambda <- result_step5$best_params$lambda
best_logloss <- result_step5$best_logloss

# Update the parameters with the best found values
cat(sprintf("\nBest parameters: alpha = %.1f, lambda = %.1f, Logloss: %.4f\n", 
            best_alpha, best_lambda, best_logloss))

fixed_params$alpha <- best_alpha
fixed_params$lambda <- best_lambda

# Plot the results as a line plot
best_combination_index <- which.min(logloss_results$logloss)

ggplot(logloss_results, aes(x = combination, y = logloss, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  # Line plot for log-loss
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Points for each combination
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Highlight best combination
  annotate("text", x = 4, y = best_logloss, 
           label = paste("Best:  ", best_alpha, ";", best_lambda), 
           vjust = -1, color = "red", size = 4) +  # Label for best combination
  labs(
    title = "Logloss vs. Parameter Combination",
    x = "Combination (alpha ; lambda)",
    y = "Logloss"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### Step 6: learning rate (`eta`)

Reduce the learning rate to limit overfitting.

```{r}
# Step 6: Tune `eta`
param_grid_step6 <- expand.grid(eta = c(0.1, 0.06, 0.01))

result_step6 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(eta = numeric(), logloss = numeric())

  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing eta = %.3f\n", 
                i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$eta[i]))
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search param
    current_params <- c(
      fixed_params,
      list(eta = param_grid$eta[i])  # Dynamically set eta
    )
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = current_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, 
                             data.frame(eta = param_grid$eta[i], logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- list(eta = param_grid$eta[i])
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (eta = %.3f)\n", 
                  best_logloss, param_grid$eta[i]))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}

# Run the optimization for `eta`
result_step6 <- result_step6(param_grid_step6, fixed_params, xgb_train, nrounds = nrounds)

            best_eta, best_logloss))
```

### Step 7: `max_delta_step`

Tuned last because it stabilizes the optimization (useful with imbalanced classes) rather than shaping the trees.

```{r}
param_grid_step7 <- expand.grid(max_delta_step = c(0, 1, 2, 3))
set.seed(1234)
result_step7 <- function(param_grid, fixed_params, dtrain, nfold = 5, early_stopping_rounds = 10, nrounds) {
  best_logloss <- Inf
  best_params <- NULL
  logloss_results <- data.frame(max_delta_step = numeric(), logloss = numeric())
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(param_grid)) {
    cat(sprintf("Iteration %d of %d: Testing max_delta_step = %.1f\n", 
                i, nrow(param_grid), param_grid$max_delta_step[i]))
    
    # Combine fixed params with the current grid search param
    current_params <- c(
      fixed_params,
      list(max_delta_step = param_grid$max_delta_step[i])  # Dynamically set max_delta_step
    )
    
    # Perform cross-validation
    cv <- xgb.cv(
      params = current_params,
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = nrounds,
      nfold = nfold,
      early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
      maximize = FALSE,
      verbose = 0
    )
    
    mean_logloss <- min(cv$evaluation_log$test_mlogloss_mean)
    logloss_results <- rbind(logloss_results, 
                             data.frame(max_delta_step = param_grid$max_delta_step[i], logloss = mean_logloss))
    
    if (mean_logloss < best_logloss) {
      best_logloss <- mean_logloss
      best_params <- list(max_delta_step = param_grid$max_delta_step[i])
      cat(sprintf("New best logloss found: %.4f (max_delta_step = %.1f)\n", 
                  best_logloss, param_grid$max_delta_step[i]))
    }
  }
  
  list(best_params = best_params, best_logloss = best_logloss, logloss_results = logloss_results)
}
```

## Final training and number of rounds

Train with the tuned parameters, tracking train and validation log-loss; early stopping on the validation set refines the number of rounds.

```{r}
# Final model training with best parameters
xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  params = fixed_params,
  data = xgb_train,
  watchlist = list(train = xgb_train, eval = xgb_validation),
  nrounds = nrounds,
  early_stopping_rounds = 300,
  print_every_n = 100
)

```

Best number of boosting rounds and training vs validation log-loss curves.

```{r}
head(evaluation_log)

  scale_color_manual(name = "Dataset", values = c("Train" = "blue", "Validation" = "red")) +
```

## XGBoost predictions

Predictions on the validation set: class probabilities, predicted class (highest probability) and accuracy.

```{r}
xgb_preds <- predict(xgb_model, as.matrix(X_validation), reshape = TRUE)
xgb_preds <- as.data.frame(xgb_preds)
data_new$Target <- as.factor(data_new$Target)

levels(data_new$Target)

colnames(xgb_preds) <- levels(data_new$Target)
# head(xgb_preds)
####################################################
xgb_preds$PredictedClass <- apply(xgb_preds, 1, function(y) colnames(xgb_preds)[which.max(y)])
xgb_preds$ActualClass <- levels(data_new$Target)[y_validation + 1]
# xgb_preds
# head(xgb_preds)
accuracy <- sum(xgb_preds$PredictedClass == xgb_preds$ActualClass) / nrow(xgb_preds)
accuracy

# NOTE: here the arguments are in (actual, predicted) order; the test-set chunk below uses (predicted, actual)
confusionMatrix(factor(xgb_preds$ActualClass), factor(xgb_preds$PredictedClass))
```

```{r}
xgb_preds_test$PredictedClass <- apply(xgb_preds_test, 1, function(y) colnames(xgb_preds_test)[which.max(y)])
xgb_preds_test$ActualClass <- levels(data_new$Target)[y_test + 1]
# xgb_preds_test

# head(xgb_preds_test)
accuracy <- sum(xgb_preds_test$PredictedClass == xgb_preds_test$ActualClass) / nrow(xgb_preds_test)
accuracy


confusionMatrix(factor(xgb_preds_test$ActualClass), factor(xgb_preds_test$PredictedClass))
```

Confusion matrix on the test set (predicted vs actual) and normalized plot.

```{r}
confusion_matrix_xgb <- confusionMatrix(factor(xgb_preds_test$PredictedClass), factor(xgb_preds_test$ActualClass))
print(confusion_matrix_xgb)

# Convert the confusion matrix to a data frame
cf_xgb_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(confusion_matrix_xgb))
colnames(cf_xgb_df) <- c("Predicted", "Actual", "Count")

# Sum for the actual labels
sums <- tapply(cf_xgb_df$Count, cf_xgb_df$Actual, sum)

# Percentages
cf_xgb_df$Percentage <- cf_xgb_df$Count / sums[cf_xgb_df$Actual] * 100

# Display the normalized confusion matrix with ggplot
ggplot(cf_xgb_df, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted, fill = Percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "lightpink") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Actual", y = "Predicted", title = "Normalized Confusion Matrix")

```

## XGBoost variable importance

Variable importance (built-in plot, top 10).

```{r}
# Compute variable importance
importance_matrix <- xgb.importance(feature_names = colnames(xgb_train), model = xgb_model)

# Plot variable importance
xgb.plot.importance(importance_matrix, top_n = 10, col = rainbow(10))  # top_n sets the number of variables to show
```

Top 10 features by Cover.

```{r}
# Convert importance matrix to a data frame
importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance_matrix)

# Sort by Cover (Gini importance) in descending order
importance_df <- importance_df[order(-importance_df$Cover), ]

# Create the plot for the top 10 features
ggplot(importance_df[1:10, ], aes(x = reorder(Feature, Cover), y = Cover, fill = Cover)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkblue") +  # Green gradient for Gini
  labs(title = "Top 10 Features by Gini Importance (Cover)", x = "Features", y = "Importance (Cover)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

5 least important features by Cover.

```{r}
importance_matrix <- xgb.importance(feature_names = colnames(xgb_train), model = xgb_model)

# Convert to a data frame
importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance_matrix)

# Sort the variables by Cover (Gini-based importance) in ascending order
least_important <- importance_df[order(importance_df$Cover), ][1:5, ]

# Create the plot for the 5 least important variables
ggplot(least_important, aes(x = reorder(Feature, Cover), y = Cover, fill = Cover)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightgreen", high = "darkgreen") +  # Blue color scheme
  labs(title = "Least Important Features by Gini Importance (Cover))", x = "Features", y = "Importance (Cover)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
